previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, HIV/AIDS, and ongoing MRSA bacteremia presented with palpitations and severe Clostridium difficile colitis. She had recently been treated with metronidazole but continued to have frequent diarrhea, leading to dehydration and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Intravenous fluids and oral vancomycin led to resolution of the arrhythmia and improvement in bowel symptoms. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.2, and warfarin was continued without bridging. She received hemodialysis during the admission and was discharged to an extended care facility to complete IV vancomycin for MRSA and a prolonged course of oral vancomycin for C. difficile, with close follow-up for anticoagulation and HIV management.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o F with complicated hx of poorly-controlled HIV/AIDS, 
recent MRSA bacteremia s/p IV vancomycin course through 
___, recent C-diff colitis on po vanco through ___, 
ESRD on HD via R tunneled femoral line now admitted for HA and 
malaise.  

# Malaise, HA, photophobia: Pt's initial presentation was 
concerning for possible meningitis. She refused an LP, citing 
concerns about pain, and was covered with ampicillin, 
ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir. Her cryptococcal antigen 
was negative, making cryptococcal meningitis very unlikely. Her 
symptoms improved within 24 hrs. After extensive discussions 
with the ID team and her PCP, her symptoms were felt to be 
consistent with her prior headaches, with possible contributors 
from post-herpetic neuralgia on the right and rebound from 
recent discontinuation of narcotics, exacerbated by missing an 
HD appointment. There was no evidence of recurrent MRSA 
bacteremia or Cdiff or PJP pneumonia. Immune reconstitution 
syndrome was also felt to be less likely. Discharged on a short 
course of Percocet, with further opiate/pain control issues to 
be determined by her outpatient providers. 
   
# Missed dialysis: Presented with DOE, reported hypoxia and some 
orthopnea in the setting of a missed HD session. TTE ___ wnl. 
Her symptoms resolved with HD.

# Chronic anticoagulation: Anticoagulated lifelong for presumed 
para-HD line DVT in the right iliac (subsequently replaced) and 
a fib, in the setting of perceived hypercoagubility from ESRD. 
Coumadin initially held while INR was supratherapeutic and LP 
was considered. She was not bridged. Restarted at discharge at 
lower dose of 6 mg, with next INR to be drawn at PCP ___ on 
___.
 
# HIV/AIDS: dx'd in ___: CD4=13 on ___, CD4 = 142 on 
___ VL 102k ___ 1,250 copies/ml on ___ hx PCP PNA ___ 3) 
after restarting HAART while at ___. Since returning 
home acknowledged taking her HAART only intermittently and CD4 
down to 108 during this admission. After discussion with ID, 
decision made to continue home abacavir 600mg daily, atazanavir 
300mg daily, azithromycin 1200mg weekly ritonavir 100mg daily, 
emtricitabine 200mg ___ and ___, SMZ/TMP DS ___, 
___. Restarted valacyclovir at discharge. PCP discussed with 
pt the possibility of home-observed HAART administration by the 
ID PACT program, pt will consider this.    

# ESRD ___ HIV/AIDS nephropathy on HD. Continued sevelamer 
1600mg tid with meals, cinacalcet 60mg daily 

# Hypotension: Unclear if readings are accurate given 
significant scarring of vessels in BUE. Given that she was 
asymptomatic and readings at her recent baseline, no changes 
were made. She generally is ___ systolic, 70s after HD. 
Continued home midodrine 5mg PO TID.
  
# MRSA bacteremia ___ to HD tunneled line infection: s/p IV 
vanco course which ended ___.  

# Clostridium difficile colitis: Discontinued PO vancomycin per 
PCP recommendation given that she no longer has diarrhea. 

# Eosinophilia: Undergoing work up with Dr. ___ as outpatient, 
longstanding, thought to possibly be ___ longstanding poorly 
controlled HIV.
  
# Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: Coumadin as above. Generally 
in sinus rhythm during this admission except during HD on the 
day of discharge (see below). Not on rate control as an 
outpatient.

# Right V1 herpes zoster ___ complicated by post-herpetic 
neuralgia and decreased vision in the right eye: Valacyclovir as 
above.  

# Hypercalcemia: Rising during this admission. ___ be ___ 
hypervitaminosis D and hyperparathyroidism. Vitamin D with HD 
held and given low-cal HD bath. Cinacalcet continued. 
Considerations can be made for multiple myeloma or granulomatous 
disease if initial work up is negative as an outpatient.

# Blurry vision: Pt noted L blurry vision x2-3 weeks without eye 
pain, in the setting of baseline R vision loss from zoster. 
Optho eval revealed presbyopia, recommended corrective lenses. 
Pt should followup with optho as ___.

# Chest tightness: On the day of discharge pt noted sense of 
chest pressure and fluttering at initiation of HD. EKG with 
atrial fibrillation without or RVR or ischemic changes. This was 
felt to be the likely cause of her symptoms as her symptoms 
resolved once back in sinus rhythm. If symptoms recur, referral 
for stress or Holter can be considered.
